name: Pointer by Purple Daddy
tagline: Aim your iPhone at your Mac and the cursor follows.
platforms: iPhone (works with a free Mac app)
status: TestFlight beta (not on the public App Store yet)
about:
Pointer turns your iPhone into a remote pointer for your Mac. You aim the phone at the screen and the cursor goes there; tap to click, press and hold to drag, two-finger tap to right-click. It works with the Pointer Mac app, which is a separate download.

There is no account and no server. The iPhone and the Mac talk directly over Bluetooth.

collects.what: Pairing key for each Mac you allow
collects.where: On your iPhone and on your Mac
collects.why: So only phones you approve can control the Mac.

usage_data: Pointer keeps a small activity log on your iPhone for troubleshooting. It records what the app was doing and errors, and it is not uploaded anywhere by the app. There is no send-to-support feature in this version.
not_collected: No tracking across other apps or websites
No analytics or crash-reporting tools from other companies

permissions.name: Bluetooth
permissions.why: To find and talk to your Mac.

permissions.name: Motion
permissions.why: To know where the phone is aimed.

retention: Pairings and settings stay on your iPhone until you unpair a Mac or choose Settings > Erase All Data on This iPhone, which removes them and returns the app to its welcome screen. It does not change anything on your Mac; unpair there too.
children: Pointer is not made for children. It has no accounts and does not knowingly collect any data.
support_what: Pointer is a remote pointer: your iPhone controls the cursor on your Mac over Bluetooth. You need the Pointer app on your Mac (macOS 14 or later) and an iPhone with iOS 17 or later.
support_steps: Install Pointer on your Mac and open it. Allow Bluetooth.
Turn Pointer on under System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility so macOS lets it move the cursor.
Open Pointer on your iPhone and follow the welcome screen.
Choose your Mac from the list, allow the iPhone on the Mac, then point at the middle of the screen and tap Center.

support_faq.a: Open Help in the iPhone app and run the self-check. Make sure the Mac app is open, Bluetooth is on for both, and Pointer is allowed under Accessibility on the Mac.

support_faq.q: How do I unpair a Mac?
support_faq.a: In Settings on the iPhone, unpair the Mac. Remove the iPhone on the Mac too.
No. The phone and the Mac talk over Bluetooth only.

support_faq.q: How do I contact the developer?
support_faq.a: Open an issue on the developer's GitHub page for the apps (linked from the apps index), or send TestFlight feedback from the TestFlight app.
